madretsch.title: The Waqf Project
madretsch.excerpt: Madretsch Islamic Cultural Centre, City of Biel
madretsch.subtitle: Madretsch Islamic Cultural Centre, City of Biel
madretsch.intro: A longstanding Islamic beacon, and the first mihrab where prayer was established in the city of Biel, canton of Bern, this is not merely a building, but a strategic waqf that combines worship with education and financial sustainability, remaining a unifying home and a lasting impact for generations.
objectifs: Financial and developmental independence: preserving the waqf and sustaining its lasting impact.
Caring for religious practice: providing a suitable spiritual environment for worship, in accordance with applicable laws and frameworks.
Education and knowledge development: strengthening community connection and cultural support for young people.
The practical embodiment of coexistence and citizenship values: activating the role of Muslims in positively contributing to society.
description: One of the oldest centres in the region, founded to be a home for everyone, it officially became an Islamic waqf in 2009 to ensure the continuity of its impact.
The project combines the mosque (offered free of charge to Muslims) with a stable rental income, generating a steady financial resource that covers operations and maintenance independently.
The building underwent a comprehensive renovation in 2020 to ensure the quality of its facilities and the effectiveness of its mission for the long term.
madretsch.avancement: Help complete this impact: a project that has undergone a comprehensive renovation to serve our generations, and covering its remaining costs is today a responsibility resting on us. Your contribution closes this debt and ensures the sustainability of the beacon.
madretsch.vision: For the centre to become a sustainable waqf model, an Islamic beacon combining the authenticity of worship, excellence in knowledge, and positive citizenship within the city.

headings.intro: An impact that endures... a giving that is renewed

madretsch.message: A vibrant spiritual and social space that embodies the values of coexistence and serves our diverse minority. The place is provided to Muslims in the city free of rent, to ensure the sustainability of this giving, and to be a unifying home where everyone finds the shade of brotherhood and community services.

aliman.title: Al Iman Islamic Cultural Centre (Fribourg)
aliman.excerpt: A symbol of openness and diversity
aliman.subtitle: A symbol of openness and diversity
aliman.intro: The founding of the “Al Iman Centre” in 2018 was not merely a property addition, but the embodiment of a waqf philosophy that goes beyond walls to establish a lasting human impact. A unifying home that erases ethnic and gender differences, and a living symbol of unity and complementarity in service of the common good of Muslims.
objectifs: Preserving Islamic identity and nurturing the cultural specificity of the Albanian minority and rising generations.
Activating the principle of the “single body” to serve all Muslims and promote positive diversity within society.
Providing an integrated, competent system covering religious, educational and social aspects.
Bringing modern waqf to life through an exemplary strategic partnership with the Albanian Cultural Association (CCA).
Making the waqf a platform for community solidarity and anchoring the unity of human impact and joint action.
aliman.avancement: In line with the foundation's vision of sustainability, daily operations and outreach activities are managed by the Albanian Cultural Association (CCA), a partner that ensures the waqf is activated to its fullest potential and connected to the real needs of the local community.
aliman.vision: A pioneering waqf model that goes beyond bricks and mortar to build a civilizational partnership; it safeguards the identity of the younger generation, reflects the open essence of Islam, and offers sustainable solutions that strengthen our positive presence in society.

headings.intro: Foreword: a vision beyond bricks and mortar
headings.strengths: The strategic importance of the Al Iman Centre

strengths: A cradle of identity: it anchors the spiritual and cultural values of the Albanian minority in Fribourg and preserves the identity of rising generations.
Bridges of openness: it extends its services and guidance to all Muslims in the city, embodying the concept of mutual solidarity and a single body.
Competence and integration: it offers a comprehensive system (religious, educational and social) with high capability, proving that great impact is not defined by the size of a space.

albadr.title: Al Badr Centre
albadr.excerptHome: The only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France: renovation of a historic building from 1902.
albadr.excerpt: The only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France: renovation of a historic building from 1902 and an extension of 1,400 m² for a large Islamic cultural centre.
albadr.subtitle: The only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France
albadr.intro: The Al Badr Centre in Le Locle is a project of singular scale: on a plot of 2,029 m², of which 600 m² are already built and 1,400 m² are set aside for the extension, it is the only mosque on the border between Switzerland and France. The existing building, put up in 1902, is of remarkable architectural interest.
objectifs: Complete renovation of the historic building from 1902
Modern construction of an extension of 1,400 m²
Create the only Islamic cultural hub on the border between Switzerland and France
albadr.description: The Al Badr Centre is the most ambitious project of Fondation Wakef. A few steps from the French border, it serves a community unlike any other, living on both sides of that border. The project combines the preservation of a remarkable architectural heritage (the building of 1902) with a resolutely modern vision for its extension.
albadr.avancement: Phase 1 completed: the men's prayer hall (70 m²) and the women's prayer hall (60 m²) are in use. Phase 2 under way: complete renovation of the historic building and construction of the extension of 1,400 m².
albadr.vision: To make the Al Badr Centre a leading Islamic cultural centre for the communities of Le Locle and the neighbouring French regions, bringing heritage and modernity together in a place that is unique in Switzerland.

annour.title: An-Nour Centre
annour.excerpt: From a dream we drew together to a centre built in the heart of Sion: the great home that embraces our children and safeguards their identity.
annour.subtitle: An Islamic cultural centre in the heart of Sion
annour.intro: From a dream we drew together to an achievement we built, by the grace of Allah and then through the generosity of our benefactors: this is the great home that embraces our children and safeguards their identity. It stands as a bridge of connection and a cultural landmark reflecting our genuine contribution to the canton of Valais; a legacy that binds us to this land, and a present and future that bring us together with everyone.
annour.objectifs: To establish a cultural space that strengthens the spiritual values of Muslims and nurtures their younger generations to become constructive members of their society, while preserving their religious dignity and activating the developmental impact of the waqf.

fiche.label: Phase 2
fiche.value: 210 m², promise of sale until the end of 2026

annour.description: Towards institutional stability that preserves values, strengthens solidarity and makes the Muslim presence a positive asset for peaceful coexistence, through waqf ownership that ensures sustainability and keeps resources from being wasted on temporary solutions.
avancement: Phase 1 (completed, by the grace of Allah): acquisition of the first part of the property, covering 210 m².
Phase 2 (in progress until the end of 2026): signing a promise of sale to acquire an adjoining 210 m² space and increase capacity.
annour.vision: A leading waqf institution that preserves values, nurtures people and actively contributes to enriching cultural diversity and social harmony.
strengths: A strategic, flexible location: the project sits in an area that allows complete flexibility for a wide range of activities and events.
A geographic first: it is the first Arabic speaking cultural centre to meet the needs of the community in Sion, the cantonal capital.
Lasting impact: waqf ownership that preserves resources and secures institutional stability, supporting peaceful coexistence and strengthening community solidarity.
annour.appel: Your contribution today creates lasting impact and helps complete this blessed project.

bibliotheque.title: Mobile Library
bibliotheque.excerpt: “Ponts du Savoir” (Bridges of Knowledge): a multilingual travelling library that fosters intercultural dialogue. Slogan: “Let us get to know one another. Knowledge brings us together.”
bibliotheque.subtitle: “Ponts du Savoir” (Bridges of Knowledge): knowledge brings us together
bibliotheque.intro: At the heart of the contemporary European setting, and more precisely within the distinctive social and cultural context of the Swiss Confederation, this project sets out as a quality civilisational initiative and an innovative embodiment of the concept of urban cultural diplomacy.
objectifs: To create an interactive environment for exchanging ideas, free from preconceptions.
To offer quality content that connects authentic Islamic values with the issues of contemporary European society.
To address today's realities in a contemporary language drawing on the intellectual output of Europe's Muslims.
To make known the historical and human contributions of Islamic civilisation and its role in strengthening human coexistence.
bibliotheque.description: Highlighting the approach of dialogue “in the best manner”, founded on reasoned listening, beauty and mutual respect.
bibliotheque.avancement: The programme has been running since 2023. It is regularly present at cultural events and in public spaces across Romandy. The network of ambassadors keeps growing.
vision: From a platform for dialogue to growth and a lasting human model
Becoming a national network (from one vehicle to a mobile fleet):
Developing a smart application (App) that lets visitors reserve books and follow the vehicle's live location on a map (GPS).
Documenting the experience and producing a guide to best practice, so that the initiative can be passed on as an inspiring model to Muslim minorities in other European countries.
captions: Books in French on the shelves
Translations of the Quran in several languages
The shelves seen from the back

delal-el-khayr.title: Project Dilal Al Khair
delal-el-khayr.excerpt: From the burden of rent to the security of a lasting waqf
delal-el-khayr.subtitle: From the burden of rent to the security of a lasting waqf

headings.intro: "Dilal Al Khair" in Le Locle: a waqf whose good reaches beyond borders
headings.strengths: Project strengths: a lasting vision and an impact beyond borders

intro: In the heart of Le Locle, in the canton of Neuchâtel, on the strategic and lively border strip between Switzerland and France, the "Dilal Al Khair" project aims to be far more than a place of prayer: it is the only landmark in the region that builds a bridge of faith and community between Muslims and cross-border workers.
This waqf project puts a lasting end to years of exhausting rental, moving our efforts from scattered, temporary costs to lasting stability.
objectifs: Our spiritual goal: to provide the only place of prayer in the region, a beacon of worship and serenity.
Our sustainable goal: to make the project financially self-sufficient through steady income, and end the burden of rent.
Our social goal: to build a bridge between the two communities on the Swiss-French border, serving the younger generations.
strengths: The only mosque in the town, on the border of two countries (Switzerland and France).
Financial sustainability and self-funding, free from the burden of rent.
A strategic location with cross-border reach, where the two communities meet.
A lasting waqf: a multiplied good and an ongoing reward. Your gift today becomes a stable asset that funds itself and serves your brothers and sisters in the border region, forever.
avancement: Every day counts: we are gathering donations to reach the required budget of CHF 550'000. Every gift brings us one step closer to securing this blessed waqf, a spiritual and learning centre bringing together the Muslims of Le Locle and the surrounding area.
Your gift today: a seed of good whose fruit will benefit our future generations.
delal-el-khayr.vision: "Dilal Al Khair" is not just a building or a place of prayer: it is the founding of a lasting Islamic waqf in a unique location, where today's gift becomes a share in an everlasting good that funds itself and serves generation after generation on the Swiss-French border, forever.

hero.label: Fondation Wakef Suisse since 2009
hero.title: About the Foundation
hero.sub: A lasting gift... a mission that grows through the generations.

p1: Drawing on the solid values of Islamic solidarity, and embodying the concept of lasting waqf, Fondation Wakef Suisse was created in 2009 as an official entity subject to the provisions of Article 80 of the Swiss Civil Code (register of the canton of Vaud, number CHE-114.901.246).

The foundation carries a civilisational mission that aims to promote positive citizenship and to establish a balanced religious and educational environment. Its fields of action cover the upkeep of places of worship and support for those who run them, as well as support for scientific research and the academic empowerment of young people.

Through our investments and our quality initiatives, we seek to lay the foundations of lasting institutional work that meets the expectations of Muslims in Switzerland, and to secure for Islamic institutions a financial independence that allows giving to endure across generations.
about.p2After: refers to the Islamic concept of a perpetual endowment: an asset or a sum irrevocably devoted to a cause of public benefit, whose income serves the community generation after generation.
about.missionText: To promote positive citizenship through a balanced educational and religious framework. Our work covers the upkeep of places of worship, the training of imams, support for scientific research and academic guidance for young people.
about.visionText: Waqf is a lasting human heartbeat that seeks the pleasure of God, sowing goodness in the fabric of societies and building edifices of happiness and fulfilment for every human being.
about.messageText: To harness the values of Islamic waqf to build institutions able to meet the needs of Muslims, enabling them to contribute actively to the progress of their societies.

hero.label: One of the pillars of Islam
hero.title: Zakat
hero.sub: “And those within whose wealth is a known right, for the one who asks and the one who is deprived.” (Al Maarij, 70:24 and 25)

zakat.toolBody: Calculate your annual Zakat flexibly and accurately, in line with recognised Islamic rules. Current Nisab threshold in Switzerland: CHF 4,600 (equivalent to 85 g of gold)
zakat.belowNisab: ℹ️ Your net wealth is below the Nisab (CHF {{nisab}}). You do not owe Zakat al-Māl this year.
zakat.nisabInfo: The Nisab is calculated on the basis of 85 g of gold (about CHF 4,600). Zakat is due if your net wealth reaches this threshold and a full lunar year (the Hawl) has passed over it.
zakat.estimateNote: This calculation is an indicative estimate.

explain.title: The Nisab
explain.desc:
It is the minimum level of wealth that makes Zakat obligatory, equal to the value of 85 g of gold (or 595 g of silver).
Current value: about CHF 4,600.

explain.title: The Hawl:
explain.desc: It is the condition of time: a full lunar year (about 354 days) must pass while you hold wealth that reaches the Nisab.

explain.title: The Zakat rate (2.5%)
explain.desc: Zakat on wealth (Zakat al Māl) is calculated at 2.5% of net zakatable wealth (your total savings, less short term debts).

explain.title: What is subject to Zakat:
explain.desc:
The Zakat base: what is subject to it and what is exempt
• Zakat is due on: gold and silver; cash, liquid funds and bank accounts; shares and investment holdings (at their market value); savings and halal investments.
• Zakat is not due on: your main personal residence; your car and belongings for personal use.

faq.q: Can I pay my Zakat in several instalments?
faq.a: Yes, Zakat may be paid in several instalments over the course of the lunar year, as long as the full amount is settled before the anniversary date (Hawl). It is nevertheless better to pay it in one go, so that no deadline is forgotten.

faq.q: How do I calculate Zakat on a salary?
faq.a: For employees, Zakat is calculated on the net savings built up over the year, not on the gross salary. Work out the savings you still hold (income less necessary spending) at the end of a lunar year. If those savings exceed the Nisab, you owe 2.5% on them.

faq.q: My calculator says “Below the Nisab”: am I exempt?
faq.a: If your net wealth is below the Nisab (~CHF 4,600), you do not owe Zakat al-Māl. You may still give a voluntary Sadaqah at any time.
For entrepreneurs, property held for resale, cryptocurrencies or complex financial situations, we recommend consulting a qualified Islamic scholar or our team. Write to us at info@wakf.ch.

zakat.noteBody: Our calculator covers standard cases. For entrepreneurs, owners of commercial property, investors or unusual financial situations, our team can guide you.

hero.label: Fondation Wakef Suisse
hero.title: Frequently asked questions
hero.sub: All the answers about the Foundation, donations, Zakat and our projects. A question still unanswered? Write to us.

items.q: What is the Fondation Wakef Suisse?
items.a: The Fondation Wakef Suisse is a foundation under Swiss private law (Art. 80 CC), registered under CHE-114.901.246 and founded in 2009. It funds Islamic infrastructure projects in Switzerland: mosques, Islamic centres, scholarships and Muslim burial sections in cemeteries.
The Foundation is supervised by the Federal Supervisory Authority for Foundations. It has independent auditors who examine the accounts every year.

items.q: How large is the endowment capital?
items.a: The initial endowment capital is CHF 50,000, in accordance with the statutes registered in 2009. All the funds collected are added to this capital and are used exclusively for the projects of the Foundation.

items.q: How do I make a donation?
items.a: You can donate through our online form on the “Donate” page, by bank transfer (details available on request at info@wakf.ch), or by post to our contact office in Biel/Bienne.

items.q: Can I make a recurring (monthly) donation?
items.a: Yes. You can choose a monthly donation by saying so on the form. Our team will then contact you to set up the standing order.

items.q: Is the Foundation transparent in the way it is run?
items.a: Yes. The Fondation Wakef Suisse is subject to Swiss civil law (Art. 80 CC) and supervised by the cantonal supervisory authority for foundations of the canton of Vaud. The accounts are examined every year by independent auditors and the financial reports are available on request at info@wakf.ch.

items.q: Can I make a donation dedicated to a specific project?
items.a: Yes. When you donate, you can name the project you wish to support among our five projects: Madretsch Mosque (Biel/Bienne), Al Iman Centre (Fribourg), An-Nour Centre (Sion), Project Dilal Al Khair (Le Locle) and the Mobile Library “Ponts du Savoir”. If that project is fully funded, the money will go to the priority project under way.

items.q: How do I calculate my Zakat?
items.a: Use our Zakat calculator on the /zakat page. Enter your assets (gold, silver, liquid assets, investments) and your short term debts. If your net wealth has exceeded the Nisab (CHF/€ 4,600) for a lunar year, you owe 2.5% of that amount.
The Nisab is the minimum threshold of wealth. It is set at the value of 85g of gold, about CHF 4,600 in 2025. If your net wealth is below this threshold, you do not owe Zakat al-Māl.
Yes. Zakat al-Fitr is an obligatory act of charity paid at the end of Ramadan, whatever your wealth. Its amount is set each year by Islamic scholars (usually between CHF 10 and 20 per person).

Fondation Wakef funds five projects: Madretsch Mosque in Biel/Bienne (completed, 496 m²), Al Iman Centre in Fribourg (ongoing, 132 m²), An-Nour Centre in Sion (ongoing, 420 m²), Project Dilal Al Khair in Le Locle (ongoing) and the Mobile Library “Ponts du Savoir” in Switzerland. See the Projects page for full details.

Each donation goes to a general fund or to a specific project, according to your choice. The Foundation Board approves the allocation of the funds, and an annual report sets out the use of every franc collected.

items.q: Can I dedicate my donation to a specific project?
items.a: Yes. When you donate, you can name the project you wish to support (Madretsch Mosque, Al Iman Centre or An-Nour Centre). If that project is already funded, the money will go to the most urgent project.

hero.label: Official documents
hero.title: Statutes of the Foundation
hero.sub: The official statutes of the Fondation Wakef Suisse, registered under CHE-114.901.246 pursuant to Art. 80 CC. Adopted on 5 June 2009, amended on 13 April 2018.

statutes.cardLine2: Founded on 5 June 2009 · Amended on 13 April 2018
statutes.cardLine3: Art. 80 ss Swiss Civil Code · Registered office: Prilly (VD)

articles.contenu: Under the name “Fondation WAKEF SUISSE” (hereinafter “the Foundation”), a foundation under Swiss private law is established within the meaning of articles 80 and following of the Swiss Civil Code. The duration of the Foundation is unlimited.
The registered office of the Foundation is in Prilly, in the canton of Vaud (Switzerland).

The purpose of the Foundation is to support and fund projects of a religious, educational, social and humanitarian nature, in keeping with the values of Islam and in compliance with Swiss law. The Foundation carries out its activities exclusively in Switzerland. It pursues in particular the following objectives: (1) to build, buy and renovate Muslim places of worship; (2) to contribute to the training of imams and to their integration into Swiss society; (3) to support schools of Arabic language and Muslim culture; (4) to award scholarships to Muslim students; (5) to encourage charitable, educational, scientific and sociocultural activities; (6) to support the creation of Muslim burial sections in Swiss cemeteries.

The endowment capital is set at CHF 50,000 (fifty thousand Swiss francs) in cash. The Foundation manages this capital according to the principles of liquidity, security, return and risk spreading. This capital is inalienable and is devoted exclusively to the purposes of the Foundation.

The resources of the Foundation come from the endowment capital and its income, from gifts and legacies of natural or legal persons, from grants awarded by public or private bodies, and from any other income compatible with the purpose of the Foundation.

The members of the governing bodies of the Foundation are liable for the damage they cause intentionally or through negligence in the exercise of their functions, in accordance with the provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
The governing bodies of the Foundation are: the Foundation Board (FB), the Executive Committee (EC), also called the Bureau, the Working Group (WG), and the Auditors.

The Foundation Board is made up of 7 to 10 members, all of the Muslim faith. At least three quarters of the members must be resident in Switzerland. Members are appointed by cooptation with a two thirds majority of the serving members. Members carry out their duties on a voluntary basis.

The Foundation Board is the supreme body of the Foundation. It is competent to: define the strategic direction of the Foundation, grant signing authority on behalf of the Foundation, appoint and remove the members of the Executive Committee, approve the annual budget and the accounts, issue the internal regulations, and take any other decision reserved to the FB by these statutes.

The Foundation Board meets at least once a year. The agenda is sent to the members at least 30 days before the meeting. The quorum is reached when the majority of the members is present, necessarily including the President or the Vice President. Decisions are taken by a simple majority of the members present.

The Executive Committee (the Bureau) is made up of the President, the Vice President and the Secretary. The members of the Executive Committee are elected by the Foundation Board for a term of five years, which may be renewed.

The Executive Committee carries out the decisions of the Foundation Board and represents the Foundation towards third parties by the joint signature of two of its members. It draws up the annual budget and the balance sheet of the Foundation, and manages current business.
The Executive Committee meets at least four times a year to deal with current business and to follow the progress of the projects under way.

Any member of the Foundation Board may object to a decision of the Executive Committee within 30 days. The objection has suspensive effect and the contested decision is submitted to the Foundation Board.

The Auditors are external to and independent of the Foundation. They are appointed by the Foundation Board for a term of one year, which may be renewed. They examine the annual accounts and draw up a report for the Foundation Board and for the supervisory authority.
The financial year runs from 1 January to 31 December. The annual financial statements are submitted for approval to the Foundation Board within six months of the close of the financial year.
These statutes may be amended by a decision of the Foundation Board taken with a two thirds majority of the serving members. The purpose of the Foundation is inviolable and may not be amended.
The dissolution of the Foundation is governed by articles 88 and 89 of the Swiss Civil Code. It is ordered by the competent supervisory authority.

In the event of dissolution, the assets of the Foundation are transferred to one or more Swiss institutions under public law, or recognised as serving the public benefit, that pursue a similar purpose and are exempt from tax. This clause is inviolable. The founders irrevocably waive any right over the assets of the Foundation.

The Foundation is subject to the supervision of the competent authority in accordance with article 84 of the Swiss Civil Code and article 96 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (CRO). The Foundation may request an exemption from supervision in accordance with article 87 CC.
The Foundation is entered in the Commercial Register of the canton of Vaud.

sections.title: 1. Data controller
sections.content: The Fondation Wakef Suisse (CHE-114.901.246), Avenue de la Confrérie 11, 1008 Prilly (VD), is the controller of your personal data within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and of the Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP).

sections.title: 2. Data collected
sections.content: We collect only the data we need: surname and first name, email address, telephone number (if provided), amount and type of donation, and any information you send us through the contact form.

sections.title: 3. Purposes of the processing
sections.content: Your data is used to: process your donation and issue a tax receipt, answer your enquiries, send our newsletter (with your consent), and meet our legal obligations (tax and accounting).

sections.title: 4. Legal bases
sections.content: The processing is based on: your consent (newsletter), the performance of a contract (donations), our legal obligations (tax receipts, accounting), and our legitimate interest (security and improvement of the service).

sections.title: 5. Retention period
sections.content: Your donation data is kept for 10 years (a Swiss legal obligation). Contact data is deleted on request or after 3 years without activity. Newsletter data is deleted as soon as you unsubscribe.

sections.title: 6. Sharing of the data
sections.content: Your data is never sold. It may be shared with: Formspree (processing of the forms), Mailchimp (newsletter), and the Swiss tax authorities (for tax receipts only).

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.content: Under the GDPR and the FADP, you have the right of access, rectification, erasure, portability and objection. To exercise these rights, write to us at info@wakf.ch.

sections.title: 8. Cookies
sections.content: Our site uses only the technical cookies needed for it to work (no advertising cookies and no third party tracking). You can disable cookies in your browser.

sections.title: 9. Contact and complaints
sections.content: For any question, please write to: info@wakf.ch · +41 79 379 96 46. You may also lodge a complaint with the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).
